label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/floater.mdl, models/w_sqknest.mdl, models/w_egon.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, B, D, D where the asset was D, B, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline in all ten views is a plain cuboid on a thin base plate. The brief's control console has nothing that reads as a console form: no sloped desk face, no raised panel or bay. The controls are only painted on the front face (sides.png FRONT and FRONT-LEFT), so it reads as a cabinet.

M2.reason: The brief gives only height, 40. The measured height is 36, 10% under, inside the 15% band. Length 42 and width 28 are not asked for by the brief.

M3.reason: All three asked-for parts are present as paint: two dark-green screens (FRONT, upper half), a row of five dark switch squares (FRONT, bottom), and three amber squares standing in for dials (FRONT, middle). The dials are the weak point. At game size they read as amber squares with a mark, not as round dials, so the dial part does not read clearly.

M4.reason: The brief names no colours for the console, so this reads against its palette. The body is green-grey painted metal, the screens are dark teal glass, the dials are amber, the switches are dark, and the base is rusted. All sit in the station's palette, and each region has one clear material.

M5.reason: The screens are flat dark rectangles with no readout, glow or marking. The dials are plain amber squares with no graduations, and there are no panel lines or seams. The faces carry only a light mottle and almost no wear, so the 'worn' industrial read the brief asks for is thin.

M6.reason: Scored 2 as the brief directs for this measure. The line-up test picked the asset as the non-Valve model in 2 of 4 readings (picks A, B, D, D against the asset's positions D, B, B, D), below the three-of-four catch. Visually, though, the flat, smooth faces look plainer than the three Valve props beside it, so a player might still spot it.

M7.reason: The front is the face with screens, dials and switches, and it faces the viewer in FRONT. The console stands upright on its base plate, which sits flat in LEFT, RIGHT and BELOW.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. It has 24 triangles, well under the 422 most of Half-Life's own props of its kind spend. Every view shows a closed box with no gaps, no inside-out faces and nothing floating. The underside in BELOW is closed.
